title: The LLM Triangle: Engineering Principles for Robust AI Applications - Almog Baku:
talk_summary: Almog Baku argues LLM-native applications are 10% model and 90% data-driven engineering, and should be built like factory SOPs: interview an expert, decompose the task into explicit steps, then implement as a fixed multi-step flow rather than an open autonomous agent. He also covers model selection tradeoffs (start big, optimize down later) and context engineering (few-shot examples, relevance over volume).

takeaways.technique: SOP-decomposed fixed flows over autonomous agents
takeaways.what_they_do: They interview an expert (or act as one), extract the implicit steps, draw the process as a graph, and implement it as a fixed pipeline of small single-purpose LLM calls plus deterministic code, reserving autonomy only inside clearly bounded scopes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I highly recommend to scope uh the autonomous agents so so like they can be amazing as long as they have clear borders

takeaways.what_they_do: In the Wikipedia-writer example, raw search results are formatted to markdown by regular code before being handed to the next LLM step, so only the parts needing judgment go to a model.
takeaways.evidence_quote: some parts are done by llm and some parts are we process it using a regular software

takeaways.technique: Start with the big model, optimize down incrementally
takeaways.what_they_do: They advise starting on the largest model to collect data and understand behavior, then moving to smaller/fine-tuned models only after observing real traffic, instead of optimizing prematurely.
takeaways.evidence_quote: start with the big model collect data understand what's going on and then optimize it incrementally

takeaways.technique: Few-shot examples to encode implicit conventions
takeaways.what_they_do: They use a handful of curated examples to teach the model a desired label/vibe that is hard to describe in words, and select examples per-request by similarity or category rather than dumping all of them.
takeaways.evidence_quote: show don't tell sometimes it's easier to teach by showing and not by explaining

takeaways.technique: Right-size context: many needles, not one
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue the 'needle in a haystack' benchmark is unrealistic because real inputs contain many competing needles, so you must balance giving enough context without overloading the model.
takeaways.evidence_quote: in reality we don't really have a needle in the high stock we have a lot of H needles in a huge High stack

takeaways.what_they_do: Before building, they interview the expert to surface implicit cognitive jumps, then compile the steps into a graph, which becomes the spec for the flow.
takeaways.evidence_quote: our goal is to find the hidden implicit uh cognition jumps that the expert know but we don't
